Real estate and long signing packages

For title companies, attorneys, and private clients who need a big document package signed wherever the signers are.

Why pay me when the bank does it free?

The bank: a bank notary is great for a one-page car title. But banks often won’t take on real estate, trust, or long legal packages because of the liability. You also have to print everything yourself, find your own witnesses, and get there between 9 and 5.

With me: I go to your client’s living room, office, or coffee shop. I print the package (letter and legal), bring a full copy for the signers to keep, send scanbacks through an encrypted service, and drop the originals at FedEx for overnight delivery. You handle the closing; I handle the rest.

Prices

The price already covers mileage and basic printing inside my normal service area. Nothing is tacked on later.

Standard

One package (up to 30 pages)

$125

Includes: travel to the signing, printing one package, a clean copy for the signer, and the standard notarizations.

Several signers in one appointment

Lower rate

For example, a closing with 3 signers that would be $375 ($125 x 3) comes to $325 when it’s done in one appointment.

Included in every signing:

  • Mileage and travel: inside my normal Denver Metro service area.
  • Document Printing (printing only): Dual printing of all documents (Return Copy + Signer Copy) on the correct letter/legal paper sizes. I do not draft or prepare legal documents; I print the ones the title company or lender sends.
  • Encrypted scanbacks: I send scanbacks by encrypted, password-protected email to protect the signers’ personal and financial information.
  • Shipping: I drop the package at FedEx or UPS for overnight delivery to the title company or attorney.

If the signing stops at the table: 50%

Sometimes at a real estate or legal signing, the signers decide not to sign at the table: they disagree with the contract, have last-minute doubts, or the funds aren’t there. By then I’ve printed, driven, and blocked the time, so if the client stops the signing at the table, I charge 50% of the quoted price.

An example of how I handle it

  • The appointment: a $325 real estate package with three signers from the same family. I printed all 180 pages, showed up, and set the documents out.
  • What happened: going over the contract, the sellers saw a purchase price they didn’t agree with. Things got tense, and they said they wouldn’t sign until they talked to their attorneys.
  • What I did: I didn’t push or argue. I stayed neutral, told them respectfully to talk with their attorney, put the documents away to protect their privacy, and left. Right away I let the company that hired me know, so they could work it out.
  • How it ended: the family felt respected, the company knew everything right away, and I billed 50% ($150) for the printing and the trip.
2

Immigration attorneys: Aurora ICE facility visits

Notarizations for your clients held at the Aurora ICE Processing Center (GEO Group), as your cleared legal proxy. Every facility requires something different; here is how Aurora works.

Why me instead of the facility’s own notary?

  • Independent: I work for your firm, not the facility or its contractor.
  • On your timeline: 7 days, 8 a.m.–9 p.m., holidays included, around your deadlines.
  • In Spanish: I talk directly with your client, with no interpreter in between.
  • Your chain of custody: I bring your documents and return the signed originals straight to your office.

Aurora clearance packet:

$150per visit
  • From me: a scan of my Colorado driver’s license or state ID, plus my Notary Commission Certificate as a PDF (physical copy on request).
  • From you: your Form G-28 and a Letter of Authorization on firm letterhead naming me as your contracted legal proxy.
  • Submission: you email the packet to the visiting office or Supervisory Deportation Officer at least 24 hours in advance.
  • Visit day: I show the guards the same physical ID and go to the legal meeting room.

Price: $150 per visit (travel, clearance, and the first hour on site), $25 for each 30 minutes after that, and each notarial act separately ($15 maximum). After-hours (+$20, 7 PM–10 AM) and weekend (+$15) premiums apply on top, as on any appointment. Nothing is paid before the visit; $75 if it’s cancelled with less than 24 hours’ notice or can’t be completed.

Help for fellow notaries

For when you’re short on time or the appointment is too far away.

Apostilles at the Secretary of State

Send me your clients’ apostilles and I’ll make the trip to the Secretary of State.

Mail-in

$85Base

Includes: up to 3 documents at the Secretary of State in Denver. You overnight them to the Denver address I give you when you book, and I do the legwork.

VIP

I pick them up

$115Base

Includes: up to 3 documents. I pick them up from you anywhere in the Denver Metro area.

Add-ons:

  • More documents: $10 each.
  • Colorado SOS Fees (at cost): $15 per document same-day or $5 per document standard (see below).
  • Return (standard processing): your prepaid FedEx/UPS label + $5 handling, a $45 return trip with hand delivery in the Denver Metro area, free USPS return from the State (no tracking), or pickup at our office at Tienda Salvadoreña, 5128 E Colfax Ave, for $35 (held up to 30 calendar days after notice). Tracked shipping within the U.S. from $25 or abroad from $85 (rates).

State fees: you pick the speed

Fastest
Same-Day Priority
$15per document

I hand it in at the Secretary of State before 4:30 PM, and it usually comes back that day. Good when your client has a deadline.

Standard
$5per document

The Secretary of State works in the order things come in: typically about 5–7 business days, not guaranteed. Use it when your client isn’t in a hurry.

Required: documents have to arrive already notarized by a Colorado notary. Before I go to the Secretary of State, I check every certificate (county, date, wording, signature and full stamp). If I spot a mistake, I tell you first so you can fix it before your client gets a rejection. It’s a courtesy check, not a legal review, and the fee is for the run, not the result (terms). Requirements list.

Itemized receipt: every charge gets its own line (notarization at $15 per act if any, apostille service, extra documents, State fees at cost, and shipping), so you can pass the costs straight through to your client.
